subtitle: Understand how chords create the harmonic foundation and emotional landscape of music

overview.title: The Language of Harmony
overview.text: Chords are more than finger positions—they're the emotional vocabulary of music. Understanding harmonic function and chord relationships will transform how you hear, play, and create music across any genre.

columns.title: Functional Harmony
columns.text: Learn how chords have jobs: tonic (home), dominant (tension), subdominant (departure).

columns.title: Chord Relationships
columns.text: Discover how chord progressions create musical momentum and emotional arcs.

columns.title: Color and Texture
columns.text: Explore how chord voicings and extensions add sophistication and character.

topics.title: Chord Progressions

topics.title: Roman Numeral Analysis
topics.description: Learn to analyze chord functions using Roman numeral notation to understand harmonic relationships.

topics.title: Voice Leading
topics.description: Understand how individual chord tones move between chords to create smooth harmonic motion.

topics.title: Chord Substitutions
topics.description: Explore how different chords can serve the same harmonic function and add sophistication.

topics.title: Modal Interchange
topics.description: Discover how borrowing chords from parallel modes adds color and emotional depth.

topics.title: Extended Chords
topics.description: Learn the theory and application of 7th, 9th, 11th, and 13th chords in popular music.

topics.title: Secondary Dominants
topics.description: Master the technique of tonicizing other keys temporarily for harmonic interest.

topics.title: Chord Inversions
topics.description: Understand how bass note choice affects harmonic stability and melodic bass lines.

columns.title: Harmonic Analysis in C Major
columns.text:
C - Am - F - G
I - vi - IV - V (Classic "vi-IV-I-V" in disguise)

Function: Tonic → Relative minor (smooth voice leading) → Subdominant (departure) → Dominant (tension back to tonic)

columns.title: Voice Leading & Emotional Arc
columns.text:
Voice Leading: Notice how the top voice moves C→A→A→B, creating a descending line that pulls us back to C.

Emotional Arc: Stability → Introspection → Departure → Return (mirrors the lyrical content)

Why it works: Strong bass movement (C→A→F→G) with smooth inner voices.

infoSections.title: Practice Tips
items: Play progressions in different keys to understand patterns
Listen for bass movement - it often reveals harmonic function
Practice chord progressions with a metronome
Analyze songs you already know to see theory in action
